title: Nonlinear effects of digital transformation on the geographical distribution of supply chain partners
summary: Using a sample of Chinese listed firms from 2010 to 2024, this study finds an inverted U-shaped relationship between digital transformation and supply chain distance. That is, distance initially expands as digitalization increases but contracts at advanced levels of digitalization. The mechanism analysis reveals that risk perception is a common channel affecting both supplier and customer distance, whereas business concentration operates primarily on the supplier side. Further analysis shows that digital transformation has a U-shaped effect on geographical concentration and an inverted U-shaped effect on coverage breadth.

title: From Visibility to Recovery: Technology-Enabled Accounting and Accountability for Biodiversity, Species Protection and Ecological Restoration
summary: Biodiversity loss is emerging as a material governance and accountability concern, yet biodiversity reporting often remains fragmented from species protection and ecological recovery. This paper reviews the development of accounting and accountability for biodiversity protection and examines how emerging technologies can reshape biodiversity measurement, corporate governance disclosure and CSR accountability. Drawing on a literature review informed by structured searching, the paper identifies three generations of biodiversity accounting: accounting of biodiversity, focused on measurement and disclosure; accounting for biodiversity and species, focused on responsibility and non-human visibility; and accounting for biodiversity recovery, focused on intervention, restoration and rewilding. The review argues that artificial intelligence, big data analytics, blockchain, and digital platforms can strengthen the visibility, timeliness, traceability and assurance of biodiversity information, but can also introduce new risks of opacity, algorithmic bias, data fragmentation and technology-enabled greenwashing. We develop a technology-enabled accountability framework that links visibility, verification, responsibility, intervention, and recovery. The paper contributes to the emerging literature on technology-enabled corporate governance disclosure and CSR by showing how digital infrastructures can move biodiversity accounting beyond narrative disclosure towards more verifiable and outcome-oriented accountability.

title: CSR and Shared Value Models for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in the Philippines: A Scoping Review
summary: Abstract This scoping review systematically examines how Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and Creating Shared Value (CSV) are conceptualized, adapted, and implemented among Philippine micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) between 2016 and 2026. MSMEs, which account for 99.6% of registered businesses and employ two-thirds of the national workforce, remain underrepresented in mainstream sustainability scholarship despite their critical role in inclusive development. Guided by Arksey andO’Malley’s (2005) framework and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, the review synthesizes 62 sources including peer-reviewed studies, government policies, industry reports, and grey literature. Findings reveal that CSR in MSMEs is largely implicit, rooted in cultural values such as bayanihan and pakikisama, while CSV is emerging as a strategic framework linking social impact with business competitiveness. Documented models cluster into compliance, community-embedded, operational shared value, and supply chain collaborative approaches, each yielding economic, social, and environmental outcomes but constrained by scalability, accessibility, and measurement gaps. Evidence highlights positive impacts on profitability, employee welfare, and resource efficiency, yet remains fragmented, with limited regional diversity, gender perspectives, and longitudinal data. The study concludes by identifying priority research directions and recommending policy incentives, localized frameworks, and culturally grounded tools to strengthen MSME contributions to sustainable and inclusive growth.

title: Stakeholder perspectives on digital transformation of water and wastewater management in Turkiye
summary: ABSTRACT Digitalization enables real-time monitoring, optimization, and predictive analytics in water and wastewater management. However, gaps remain across societal, economic, governance, and research domains. This study examines stakeholder perceptions and experiences regarding the transition toward digital solutions in Turkiye’s water and wastewater sector. An online survey received 101 responses; 96 valid responses were retained for analysis. The main barriers to digital transformation include insufficient funding, limited human capacity, restrictive management practices, and data-related constraints. Mann–Whitney U analyses revealed no statistically significant differences between academic and government stakeholders regarding major digital transformation barriers, although the comparison had limited statistical power. Within each group’s own ranking, the leading perceived benefits were ensuring water quality and achieving water savings for government institutions, improving creativity, productivity, and motivation for academia; of the two benefit items presented identically to both groups, easier data exchange was valued significantly more highly by academia. Two stakeholder focus groups further identified and prioritized key barriers, including lack of standardized data management workflows, weak coordination and data sharing among stakeholders, and limited digitally skilled personnel. Recommended measures include standardized protocols, strategic workforce planning, and evidence-based governance mechanisms to support a more integrated and resilient digital water management framework in Turkiye.

title: A decision-aiding procedure for technology selection in the context of digital transformation
summary: Modern companies face the challenge of selecting suitable technologies to support a digital transformation journey. The paper presents a multi-criteria decision-aiding procedure (MCDAP) to support managers in the technology and portfolio selection processes, within a structured and practical decision-making flow. It can be used to develop a technology roadmap or select an innovation portfolio within a digital transformation journey. The Design Science Research strategy supports the paper, and the Cambridge Process Approach is used to operationalise the MCDAP in a structured and holistic process. A triangulation approach is performed for data acquisition and analysis in developing cases. An evaluation of the procedure’s feasibility, utility, and usability was obtained from the staff involved in developing cases, who considered it feasible and useful. However, improvements were recommended to enhance its usability, especially regarding the decision support system. Another relevant finding is the stated and observed need for an analyst with methodological and software knowledge. Because it has been pilot-tested in only two demonstration cases, further field testing and a careful analysis are needed to refine the procedure and apply it in other contexts, requiring a good background from managers, technical specialists, and analysts.

title: Legal reconstruction of corporate digital responsibility in the context of artificial intelligence governance
summary: The emergence of artificial intelligence now influences corporate decision-making, information processing, automatic evaluations, and relationships with stakeholders, thus raising the question of corporate digital responsibility as the subject of corporate governance. Comparative analysis addresses the possibility of transforming corporate digital responsibility from voluntary ethical commitment into legally verifiable obligation via the algorithmic lifecycle approach. The corpus consists of 18 laws, regulations, and authoritative corporate governance guidelines released during 2021-2025 and 3-4 key documents of each of the 15 selected digital companies in the European Union, China, and the United States. Twenty indicators were coded in the following categories: data governance, fairness control, transparency, human oversight, and audit/ remedy. Every indicator includes absence of commitment, general commitment, and verifiable procedures, while legal requirement-responsibility indicator-scoring basis matrix provides the link between corporate data and normative requirement. The findings reveal that transparency, human oversight, and audit/ remedy are characterized by significant differences among jurisdictions, while data governance and fairness control are more alike. The median score for audit/remedy is 75.0 in the European Union and 50.0 in China and the United States. These findings support lifecycle-based legal reconstruction connecting corporate digital responsibility with identifiable duties of care, disclosure, oversight, auditing, correction, and compensation through a framework.

title: Reinventing a Traditional Bank: A Case Study on DBS Bank's Digital Transformation
summary: Reinventing a Traditional Bank: A Case Study on DBS Bank’s Digital Transformation 1. Introduction Most banks talk about digital transformation, but very few demonstrate its value through financial metrics. DBS Bank of Singapore is an exception. Headquartered in Singapore and recognized as the largest bank in Southeast Asia, DBS managed to fundamentally rewire its operations, culture, and technology stack. This case study examines why DBS transformed, how it executed its strategy, and the lessons learned from its successes and operational hurdles. Note on Assumptions: This case study is constructed entirely from publicly available sources. Currency figures are in Singapore dollars (S$). Attributing profit growth solely to digital transformation is complex due to macroeconomic cycles; the link is treated as strong strategic evidence. 2. Main Content/Body 2.1 Why DBS Decided to Transform Around 2014, leadership under CEO Piyush Gupta realized that traditional banking competitors were no longer their primary threat. Instead, technology giants like Google, Amazon, Netflix, and Apple were setting new consumer expectations. DBS launched its transformation in 2014 with the goal of "making banking joyful" by behaving like a technology company with a banking license. 2.2 The Strategy: Project GANDALF DBS encapsulated its vision in the acronym GANDALF (Google, Amazon, Netflix, Apple, LinkedIn, and Facebook, with 'D' representing DBS). Key strategic shifts included: Google: Adopting open-source software and modern developer tools. Amazon: Migrating core workloads to secure cloud infrastructure. Netflix: Utilizing advanced data analytics and continuous experimentation. The board backed this ambition with an initial S$200 million injection into technology spending, accepting short-term efficiency impacts. 2.3 Core Process Transformation Customer Onboarding: Launched digibank in India (2016) as a mobile-only, paperless, signatureless bank supported by AI virtual assistants. AI Integration: By 2025, data analytics and AI models generated roughly S$1 billion in economic value, earning DBS accolades such as Global Finance's World's Best AI Bank. Culture: Transitioned from a meeting-heavy hierarchy to agile, startup-style cross-functional teams. 2.4 Critical Analysis: Advantages vs. Disadvantages Financial Impact: Total income expanded from S9.6 billion (2014) to S22.9 billion (2025), while the cost-to-income ratio optimized from 45.4% down to ~40.4%. Digital customers consistently delivered higher returns on equity (27%) compared to traditional customers (18%). Operational Challenges: System outages in 2021 and 2023 led the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) to impose significant additional capital requirements and temporary IT freezes. This highlighted a vital lesson: regulators treat digital platform outages as severe operational-risk and capital issues. 3. Conclusion & Key Learnings DBS proves that incumbent financial institutions can successfully reinvent themselves if transformation is championed from the top and embedded into the back-end architecture, data layers, and corporate culture. Key Takeaways for Readers: Transform the back end, not just the front-end application. Rigorously measure the financial value of digital initiatives. Culture and agile working habits are just as important as code. Build robust operational resilience alongside innovation to prevent costly regulatory penalties. 4. References DBS Bank. (2016). DBS launches India's first mobile-only bank. DBS Group Holdings. (2026). Full-year financial results and Annual Report. Monetary Authority of Singapore. (2023). MAS imposes further additional capital requirement on DBS Bank.

title: Role of Sustainable Governance Strategies in Mitigating Cross-Cultural Diversity and Economic Impacts
summary: This research investigates the function of sustainable governance approaches in alleviating difficulties related to cross-cultural diversity and economic effects in globalised and digitally interconnected settings. It examines the ways in which environmental, social, and governance principles, inclusive leadership, stakeholder engagement, cultural intelligence, and digital technology might enhance institutional legitimacy, economic resilience, and social cohesion. A qualitative exploratory framework was utilised, leveraging secondary data from scholarly articles, governance reports, policy documents, and comparative analyses in the sectors of tourism, banking, manufacturing, mining, and public administration. The information was examined using topic synthesis and inter-industry comparison to discern governance approaches, obstacles to implementation, and sector-specific results. The results suggest that culturally responsive governance, clear decision-making processes, multilingual dialogue, conflict resolution strategies, and inclusive stakeholder participation enhance organisational unity, policy endorsement, and employee retention. ESG-focused methods enhance investor trust, moral responsibility, and sustainable economic outcomes. Nevertheless, varying reporting standards, digital disenfranchisement, legal ambiguity, algorithmic prejudice, and conflicts between global sustainability principles and local cultural values hinder efficacy. The research determines that sustainable governance must incorporate ESG principles, culturally attuned policies, and digital governance within flexible, participatory structures. This integration allows institutions to harmonise economic goals with cultural authenticity, social equity, technical responsibility, and enduring resilience in many national and organisational settings.

title: Bridging the Capacity Deficit in Zimbabwe's Power-Distribution Infrastructure: A Strategic Decision-Making Analysis for emerging organisations
summary: Zimbabwe’s power-distribution infrastructure faces a persistent capacity deficit, particularly in the supply of transformers required to expand electricity access, replace ageing and vandalised infrastructure, and respond to disruption-induced demand. National requirements are estimated at approximately 6,000 transformers annually, while domestic production has historically remained at about 2,500–3,000 units, creating a substantial supply gap with implications for education, healthcare, industry, rural electrification and national development. This paper examines how emerging organisations can apply strategic decision-making to respond to infrastructure capacity deficits, using Ringfair International (Pvt) Ltd, a Zimbabwean supplier of transformers and power-line materials, as the focal organisational case. The study adopts a conceptual and theory-building approach, drawing exclusively on secondary evidence from peer-reviewed literature, government and institutional reports, utility disclosures, policy documents and credible sectoral sources. The analysis is theoretically informed by the Resource-Based View, Dynamic Capabilities Theory, Institutional Theory, Effectuation Theory, Resource Dependence Theory, Supply Chain Resilience Theory, Transaction Cost Economics, Principal–Agent Theory and Diffusion of Innovation Theory. The synthesis indicates that Zimbabwe’s transformer deficit is structural rather than temporary, reflecting constrained production capacity, ageing infrastructure, vandalism, procurement failures, financing constraints and disruption-induced demand. It further demonstrates conceptually that emerging private-sector organisations can contribute to narrowing infrastructure capacity gaps by strategically orchestrating financial resources, supplier networks, logistics capabilities, innovation and institutional relationships. Drawing these theoretical and contextual insights together, the paper develops the Agile Supply-Gap Integration (ASGI) Framework, comprising five interconnected stages: gap identification, theoretical filtering, resource mobilisation, adaptive execution and governance review. The paper concludes that infrastructure capacity deficits require adaptive, resource-conscious and institutionally responsive strategic decision-making and proposes the ASGI Framework as a conceptual tool for emerging organisations operating in resource-constrained and institutionally complex environments.

title: Tactical and Methodological Arsenal of Crime Investigation in the Context of Digital Transformation: Innovative Approaches
summary: The article examines the impact of digital transformation on the fundamental foundations of crime investigation. The thesis is substantiated that modern challenges require not just the addition of new “digital” elements to the traditional forensic arsenal, but a systemic restructuring of the investigation model itself. The key directions of this transformation are analyzed: the transition from reactive to proactive tactics, the integration of network analysis and predictive modeling, and the changing role of the investigator in a hybrid (physical-digital) environment. The purpose of the article is to identify the key areas of transformation of the tactical and methodological arsenal under the influence of the digital environment and formulate the principles of innovative approaches that can ensure eff ective counteraction to modern crime. A systematic transformation of the basic model of the investigation is needed, a revision of its principles — from the sources of information and the logic of building versions to the tactics of individual investigative actions and the role of the investigator himself. This article is an attempt to conceptualize this process. The author’s concept of the evolution of the tactical and methodological arsenal is proposed, focused on the management of information flows and the symbiosis of procedural actions with the analytical processing of big data.

title: Corruption Perception and Firm Performance: Evidence from High-Polluting Listed Companies in South Africa
summary: The corruption remains a persistent challenge that distort firm financial performance by increasing operational costs, distorting resource allocation and weakening investor confidence. However, limited studies have been conducted to examine the impact of corruption on financial performance of companies listed in Johannesburg Stock Exchange in South Africa. Limited empirical evidence on the impact of corruption on financial performance in firms listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange many result in policy and governance frameworks that are not evidence-based, limiting the interventions aimed at improving curbing corruption and improving financial performance with JSE-listed companies. This study explores how corruption perception impacts the financial performance of high-polluting companies listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) for the period 2015 to 2025. The corruption perception index was obtained from the transparency international corruption perception. The financial data and corporate governance data were companies’ annual financial reports/integrated reports. Corruption perception is measured using the Corruption Perception Index (CPI), while firm performance is proxied by return on assets (ROA) and Tobin’s Q. Board independence and board gender diversity are included as governance control variables. The study then utilises the System Generalised Method of Moments (GMM) for establishing the correlation between corruption perception and financial performance. Study’s findings reports that corruption is negatively related to financial performance. The results reveal stronger positive correlation between corporate and firm performance. The findings reveal that corporate governance could enhance firm financial performance while corruption perception impairs firm performance. The present study suggests that high polluting-companies listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange need more robust corporate governance mechanisms to curb corruption practices and to improve firm performance.

title: Competition Law as a Guiding Discipline for the Digital Economy: Submissions for the 4th Early Career Scholars' Conference in Competition Law
summary: This compilation of the working papers brings together submissions by early-career scholars (ECRs) for the 4th annual young scholars conference “Competition Law as a Guiding Discipline for the Digital Economy”, co-organised by the University of Glasgow/CREATe in collaboration with the University College London and the University of Vienna. The key questions that the ECRs were asked in preparation for the conference were: “How can competition law meaningfully support contemporary markets considering recent economic and technological changes, while using ‘out-of-the-box’ thinking? More specifically, how can this field of law foster and guide effective multidisciplinary approaches to regulate digital space for the benefit of wider society?” The resulting academic papers tackle these questions from different perspectives, considering a variety of topics such as the relationship of competition law with the (digital) press and media sector; the role of competition law in ensuring openness, accessibility and competitiveness of markets and ecosystems in the age of AI; involvement of competition law in the design and operation of regulatory sandboxes; and deploying conventional and non-conventional (enforcement) tools to support competition law analysis for the robustness of digital markets. While still works in progress, these papers offer interesting and diverse viewpoints, contributing to a wider academic debate on how best to utilise competition law in a ‘non-traditional’ way to further foster the digital economy.

title: Shadow banks on the rise: Evidence across market segments
summary: This paper examines the comparative advantages of shadow banks across market segments. Combining credit bureau data on retail loans in India with weather shocks as a proxy for credit demand, we show that Fintechs respond more in uncollateralized markets. In contrast, non-Fintech shadow banks exhibit stronger responsiveness in collateralized markets. Exploiting geographic heterogeneity in the adoption of digital payments, we identify technology as the key advantage for Fintechs. Leveraging four natural experiments, we document the significance of lower regulation for non-Fintech shadow banks. Our results suggest that the comparative advantage of shadow banks differs across market segments.

title: Theoretical Mechanism and Statistical Measurement of Integrated Development Between the Digital Economy and Modern Finance: Empirical Evidence from China
summary: Advancing the deep integration of the digital economy and modern finance is a core strategic pathway for fostering new-quality productive forces and building a modern financial system. Scientifically evaluating the level of integrated development between the two systems and clarifying its spatial evolution patterns are of great practical significance for promoting coordinated regional development and the transformation and upgrading of the financial system. Taking the integrated development of the digital economy and modern finance in China as the research subject, this paper elaborates on the mechanisms of their bidirectional integration and identifies the development level, spatial patterns, and dynamic evolution laws of such integration. Based on panel data of 30 provincial-level administrative regions in China from 2011 to 2024, this paper conducts empirical analysis using the Coupling Coordination Degree (CCD) Model, Dagum Gini Coefficient Decomposition, Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) and Spatial Markov Chain, and constructs an evaluation index system for their integrated development across four dimensions: Basic Service Integration, Innovation Momentum and Efficiency Integration, Industrial Governance Integration, and Application Scenario and Openness Integration. The research finds that the level of integrated development of China’s digital economy and modern finance has improved steadily, but remains in the primary development stage overall. Spatially, it presents a gradient pattern of “eastern leadership, central catch-up, western lagging”. Dimensionally, it features a “three strong, one weak” structural pattern, with the lag in Industrial Governance Integration being the core bottleneck restricting overall upgrading. The integrated development exhibits significant characteristics of path dependence, club convergence, and positive spatial association. This paper breaks through the perspective limitation of traditional research that focuses on unidirectional technology empowerment. The research conclusions can provide decision-making references for advancing regional integrated upgrading in a targeted manner, addressing the bottleneck of industrial governance integration, and facilitating coordinated regional development.

title: Digital Transformation, Organisational Agility and Sustainable Performance of Manufacturing SMEs in North Central Nigeria
summary: Digital transformation is increasingly important to the ability of manufacturing small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to respond to changing business conditions and sustain organisational performance. However, the relationship between digital transformation and sustainable performance may depend on the organisational capabilities through which digital resources are utilised. This study examined the relationship between digital transformation and sustainable performance among manufacturing SMEs in North Central Nigeria, with organisational agility examined as a mediating mechanism. The study was anchored on Dynamic Capabilities Theory and Absorptive Capacity Theory. A quantitative, cross-sectional survey design was adopted. From a target population of 161,313 manufacturing SMEs, a sample of 757 firms was determined, and 547 valid responses were used for analysis.

title: Emerging Technologies and Digital Transformation in South African TVET Colleges: A Narrative Literature Review
summary: This paper examines the influence of emerging technologies and digital transformation on South African Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) colleges and evaluates their implications for institutional readiness, skills development, employability and digital inclusion. The study seeks to provide an integrated understanding of the opportunities and challenges associated with technology-driven transformation in vocational education. A qualitative narrative literature review design was employed to analyse contemporary evidence on digital transformation within the TVET sector. The review drew on twenty-one peer-reviewed journal articles, policy documents and institutional reports published between 2020 and 2025, supplemented by foundational theoretical sources. Data were analysed using thematic analysis to identify dominant themes, recurring patterns and emerging trends. The findings indicate that emerging technologies, including digital learning platforms, cloud-based systems, simulation technologies, artificial intelligence and data-driven tools, are increasingly transforming teaching, learning and institutional operations within TVET colleges. The review further reveals that successful digital transformation is strongly influenced by institutional readiness factors such as infrastructure availability, leadership commitment, lecturer competence, governance arrangements and organisational support. Despite the potential of digital transformation to enhance skills development and graduate employability, persistent challenges related to digital inequality, limited connectivity, inadequate access to devices and varying levels of digital literacy continue to constrain inclusive participation and equitable outcomes. The study concludes that digital transformation in South African TVET colleges extends beyond technology adoption and requires coordinated investment in infrastructure, human capability development, curriculum reform and inclusive policy interventions. The paper contributes to the literature by synthesising current evidence on the technological, organisational and socio-economic factors shaping digital transformation in vocational education.

title: Aligning institutions and organizations for sustainable supply chains: the role of digital transformation and low-carbon practices
summary: Purpose The transition toward carbon neutrality has become a global strategic priority for achieving sustainable development and a green economy. Despite growing interest in digital transformation among scholars and practitioners, achieving a balance between green supply chain performance and carbon performance within the context of carbon neutrality remains underexplored. Drawing on the technology acceptance model and change management theory, this research aims to provide solutions for achieving the zero-carbon target in 2060 through holistic digital transformation, and how institutional pressure and organizational readiness influence green supply chain and carbon performance through digital transformation, low-carbon operations management practices (LCOMP) and the moderating role of environmental proactivity. Design/methodology/approach Data from 442 Chinese manufacturing firms were analyzed using Smart PLS v4 to test the research hypotheses. Findings The results indicate that all three dimensions of LCOMP mediate the relationship between digital transformation, green supply chain and carbon performance. In addition, environmental proactivity strengthens the influence of digital transformation on the three dimensions of LCOMP. Originality/value The findings contribute to the literature by addressing a key gap in sustainable supply chain and digital transformation research, which has largely examined these relationships in isolation without fully explaining the mediating mechanisms and boundary conditions.

title: Minority Shareholder Protection under Zimbabwe’s Companies and Other Business Entities Act (2019): A Conceptual and Theoretical Analysis of Majority Rule and Investor Safeguard
summary: This paper examines minority shareholder protection under Zimbabwe’s Companies and Other Business Entities Act [Chapter 24:31] (2019) (COBE), with the aim of evaluating how effectively the statutory framework balances majority rule with investor safeguards. Against the backdrop of recurring and highly publicised shareholder disputes in Zimbabwean companies, the study seeks to determine whether COBE provides meaningful and enforceable protection for minority shareholders within the country’s institutional context. The study adopts a qualitative, doctrinal, and conceptual research design based on documentary analysis of COBE. Using an inductive discourse-analytic approach, the Act is examined in its entirety to identify how it constructs shareholder rights, directors’ duties, governance structures, and mechanisms of redress. Rather than relying on empirical data, the analysis is theoretically grounded in agency theory, law-and-finance scholarship, and institutional theory, enabling a structured evaluation of majority minority dynamics within Zimbabwe’s corporate governance framework. The analysis reveals that COBE incorporates a range of minority-protection mechanisms, including derivative actions, remedies against oppressive conduct, disclosure obligations, and fiduciary duties imposed on directors. These provisions align, in part, with international corporate governance principles and reflect an attempt to mitigate agency conflicts between controlling shareholders, management, and minority investors. However, their practical effectiveness is constrained by structural features of majority rule, high litigation costs, judicial delays, and broader institutional limitations. The study finds that while robust minority protection can enhance investor confidence, deter opportunistic conduct, and support capital-market development, extensive safeguards may also increase compliance costs, slow decision-making, and generate risks of protracted disputes. The paper concludes that, despite identifiable drawbacks, the benefits of meaningful minority shareholder protection outweigh its disadvantages in the Zimbabwean context. The key policy challenge lies in calibrating legal safeguards to deter abuse without unduly undermining managerial efficiency and value creation. Future research could extend this conceptual analysis through empirical investigation of enforcement outcomes, comparative studies with other emerging markets, or quantitative assessment of the relationship between minority protection and capital-market development in Zimbabwe.

title: Boas práticas em serviços de alimentação e ESG trilhas da produção científica e aproximações com o turismo
summary: This study aimed to map the paths of scientific production that articulate good practices in food services and ESG (Environmental, Social and Governance) axes, through bibliometric analysis and a systematic literature review. The relationship with tourism was established by recognizing food services as activities integrated into the dynamics of destinations, the tourist experience, and sustainability. The findings indicate that, although there is scientific production on food services, there is still a scarcity of studies that relate, in an integrated way, good practices, food services, and ESG. Bibliometric analysis and the systematic review, which deepened the analysis based on the only open-access study with two of the three searched terms, highlighted the incipient nature of the field. It is identified that there is a relevant theoretical gap and possibilities for rapprochement between good practices, ESG, and food services, especially in tourism, due to the territorial, sociocultural, environmental, and managerial impacts of these enterprises on destinations.

title: DIVIDEND PAYMENT AND EARNINGS QUALITY OF LISTED DEPOSIT MONEY BANKS IN NIGERIA
summary: This study examines the effect of dividend payment on earnings quality of listed deposit money banks in Nigeria. Specifically, the study investigates the influence of dividend payout ratio, dividend paying status, and dividend yield on earnings quality. The study adopts an ex-post facto research design using panel data obtained from the audited annual reports of thirteen listed deposit money banks in Nigeria over the period 2011–2025. Earnings quality was proxied using discretionary accruals, while dividend policy was measured through dividend payout ratio, dividend paying status, and dividend yield. The study employed descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and panel regression techniques to analyze the data. Findings reveal that dividend paying status has a positive and statistically significant effect on earnings quality, suggesting that firms that consistently pay dividends are more likely to report high-quality earnings. However, dividend payout ratio and dividend yield exhibit negative but insignificant relationships with earnings quality. The findings support dividend signaling theory and agency theory, indicating that dividend payments serve as credible signals of sustainable financial performance. The study concludes that dividend- paying firms exhibit stronger earnings quality than non-dividend-paying firms among Nigerian deposit money banks. The study recommends that bank managers should maintain sustainable dividend policies supported by genuine earnings performance rather than aggressive earnings management practices. Regulators should also strengthen monitoring mechanisms to improve transparency and earnings reliability within the Nigerian banking sector. title: An approach to assessing the risks of restaurant businesses based on a scientific and methodological framework in the context of the industry’s digital transformation
summary: The article substantiates the need for a special approach to risk assessment in the restaurant business in the context of the digital transformation of the industry. A study of current digitalization trends in public catering has made it possible to identify new categories of risks caused by the introduction of digital technologies: technological, operational, regulatory, and reputational. The author presents an original methodology that combines traditional risk management with industry-specific features and digital factors. The methodological framework relies on multi-factor analysis, a risk matrix, and scenario modeling. The proposed risk assessment matrix can be practically applied by restaurant enterprises in building risk management systems.

title: Digital Transformation and Green Marketing Strategy in Shaping Consumer Purchase Intention: Evidence from UNIQLO Indonesia
summary: The rapid growth of fast fashion has worsened environmental damage through textile waste, carbon emissions, and resource use, pushing brands to adopt digital transformation and eco-focused marketing. UNIQLO is in a tricky spot: while promoting sustainability digitally, its fast fashion label raises questions about the authenticity of its environmental claims, sparking debates about its ecological accountability. This study looks at the factors that shape purchasing intentions towards UNIQLO by expanding the Theory of Planned Behaviour through environmental concern and green marketing. Using an exploratory quantitative method with PLS-SEM, data was collected from 225 UNIQLO customers in Indonesia through purposive sampling. The results show that environmental awareness, social influence, and green marketing significantly affect purchase intentions, with green marketing being the most influential, explaining 61.8% of the variation. UNIQLO should strengthen transparency and digital verification to reinforce its sustainable identity.

title: Redesigning a Sustainable Business Strategy for Traditional Snack MSMEs: An Integrated BMC and VPC Approach for Digital Transformation
summary: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) often struggle to formulate sustainable business strategies. This research aims to formulate a development strategy for Good Real Pasundan, a kerupuk gudril MSME in Pangandaran, by integrating the Business Model Canvas (BMC) and Value Proposition Canvas (VPC) frameworks. A descriptive qualitative case study approach was employed through observations, owner interviews, and a 100-respondent survey. The VPC was utilized to evaluate product-market fit by mapping customer pains and gains. The VPC analysis revealed low brand awareness and the absence of nutritional value information as primary customer pains, alongside high expectations for a consistently crispy texture and savory taste (gains). Based on these empirical findings, the initial BMC hypothesis was comprehensively revised. The resulting strategic recommendations include specifically targeting crispy and savory traditional snack lovers, strengthening the value proposition through nutritional transparency and product legality, and transforming digital distribution channels via marketplaces and social media. Ultimately, this market-verified BMC provides a robust operational roadmap for Good Real Pasundan to accelerate its competitiveness and achieve sustainable digital ecosystem growth.

title: Priority Directions of Intellectual Capital Development under Digital Transformation A Conceptual Framework and Evidence from Uzbekistan
summary: This thesis sets out priority directions for developing intellectual capital in the course of digital transformation. It combines the human-structural-relational view of intellectual capital, the idea that digital technology pays off only alongside organizational investment, and the concept of absorptive capacity. The central claim is that digital technologies create value when they are matched by skills, data and organizational structures, and by networks that spread knowledge. Uzbekistan's UN E-Government Development Index data fit this picture. The telecommunication infrastructure component rose from 0.474 in 2020 to 0.877 in 2024, whereas the education-based human capital component moved only from 0.743 to 0.758. Learning quality and digital skills therefore come first in the proposed ordering, followed by data and organizational capital, research capacity and knowledge networks.

title: Digital Transformation of E.G.G. Egg MSME through Strengthening Business Identity, Social Media Promotion, and QRIS Implementation
summary: Express, Excellent, Exclusive Genial Genial (E.G.G.) is an egg-selling MSME in Bentiring, Bengkulu City, with significant growth potential, though hindered by limitations in business identity and digital technology adoption. This community service aimed to enhance partner competitiveness through visual identity development (logos and banners), social media optimization, and integration of the Quick Response Code Indonesian Standard (QRIS) payment system. The activities encompassed problem identification, identity design, QRIS registration, and digital promotion assistance based on observation and interviews. Results indicate that the logo and banner strengthened the business's professional image, social media expanded market reach, and QRIS facilitated practical cashless transactions. The integration of these three aspects effectively supports the modernization and development of the E.G.G. MSME in the digital era.

title: A DEPENDÊNCIA DE BANKING AS A SERVICE NAS FINTECHS WHITE LABEL: IMPACTOS NA SEGURANÇA E NA CONTINUIDADE OPERACIONAL NO BRASIL
summary: O modelo white label permite que empresas ofereçam serviços financeiros sob marca própria utilizando soluções tecnológicas de terceiros. Quando associado ao Banking as a Service (BaaS), esse arranjo facilita a integração de produtos financeiros, mas também estabelece dependências relevantes para a segurança da informação e a continuidade operacional. Este artigo tem como objetivo analisar essas dependências no contexto brasileiro, distinguindo os conceitos de white label, BaaS, Open Finance e embedded finance. Adota-se uma revisão bibliográfica narrativa, de abordagem qualitativa e caráter exploratório e descritivo, com prioridade para publicações de 2024 e 2025 e apoio de documentação institucional e legislação pertinente. A discussão organiza-se em quatro eixos: configuração tecnológica e de negócios; segurança e proteção de dados; governança e conformidade; e continuidade operacional. A análise identifica benefícios potenciais de integração e expansão da oferta, acompanhados de riscos de concentração em fornecedores e de propagação de incidentes. Como encaminhamentos, propõem-se avaliação de terceiros, definição contratual de responsabilidades, monitoramento das integrações e planejamento de contingência. A adoção de múltiplos provedores é discutida como alternativa condicionada à viabilidade técnica e regulatória, sem garantia automática de continuidade. Conclui-se que a sustentabilidade do modelo exige gestão ativa das dependências e responsabilidades. Por seu caráter bibliográfico, o estudo não mensura incidentes nem testa empiricamente as estratégias propostas.

title: User-Centric Design Thinking Framework for Digital Transformation: Bridging the Digital Literacy Gap in Thai Manufacturing SMEs
summary: While digital transformation is essential for enhancing the competitiveness of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs), a significant barrier remains in the form of low levels of employees' digital literacy. This study addresses this critical challenge by proposing and validating a User-Centric Design Thinking Framework for developing digital tools in environments characterized by varying levels of technological proficiency. Using a Thai manufacturing SME as a case study, the study employed a five-stage Design Thinking process involving 20 participants to develop a web-based production management system. The methodology emphasized empathy and iterative feedback to ensure the system was intuitive, accessible, and aligned with user needs. Post-implementation analyses revealed substantial operational improvements, including an 81.1% reduction in production monitoring time and an 80.7% decrease in reporting time, accompanied by significant cost savings. Usability testing, incorporating both qualitative feedback and quantitative assessment, demonstrated a high level of user satisfaction (mean score = 4.52 out of 5). The findings indicate that a user-centric approach is effective in not only bridging the digital literacy gap but also enhancing business performance. This study provides a practical and replicable framework for technology adoption in SMEs and contributes to the broader understanding of inclusive digital transformation in developing economies.

title: The Anti‐SLAPP Statutes and Corporate Environmental Policies
summary: ABSTRACT We examine whether legal protection for civic participation affects corporate pollution. Polluters may deter public discipline through strategic lawsuits. Anti‐SLAPP (Strategic Lawsuit Against Public Participation) statutes mitigate this threat by enabling prompt dismissal and recovery of legal costs. Using a difference‐in‐differences design, we find that enacting an anti‐SLAPP statute in a state significantly reduces toxic emissions from that state by increasing local public pressure. The reduction is greater when the statutes provide stronger protection, when local stakeholders have stronger incentives and abilities to discipline polluters, and when local public pressure increases more after the enactment. Plants lower emissions by improving abatement rather than by reducing output or relocating emissions. Our paper underscores the role of legal protection in environmental governance and informs policy debates over anti‐SLAPP legislation.

title: Trade Tariffs and Corporate Greenwashing: Evidence from Chinese A-Share Listed Firms
summary: Using data on Chinese A-share firms from 2009 to 2023, we examine how import tariff exposure is related to corporate greenwashing. We combine tariff and customs data with annual reports and environmental penalty records. Greenwashing is measured by the gap between environmental disclosure and penalties relative to peers. Random-effects logit estimates show that lower tariff exposure is associated with a higher likelihood of this gap. This relationship varies with media attention, managerial incentives, and fund occupation. The findings do not prove that firms intend to mislead or that tariffs improve the environment.

title: Criteria and indicators of corporate social responsibility of enterprises in wartime conditions
summary: The article examines the criteria and indicators of corporate social responsibility under the specific conditions of wartime business operations. The study aims to substantiate and systematize criteria and indicators that can comprehensively characterize responsible corporate behavior and reflect changes in the needs and expectations of key stakeholder groups under war-related challenges. The study’s methodological framework draws on analysis and synthesis, systematization and generalization of scientific approaches, the stakeholder approach, and comparative analysis of contemporary research on corporate social responsibility in stable and crisis conditions. The study systematizes six interrelated criteria of corporate social responsibility: social and labor responsibility, economic responsibility, responsibility toward consumers and business partners, ethical and managerial responsibility, environmental responsibility, and social responsibility toward communities and society. The main indicators characterizing each area of responsible corporate behavior are identified. The wartime dimension should not be treated as an isolated area of corporate social responsibility. Instead, it should be considered as a cross-cutting characteristic that changes the content and priority of individual indicators within the established criteria. Wartime-specific manifestations include preserving employment, supporting mobilized employees and their families, ensuring business continuity, adapting business processes to war-related risks, providing humanitarian assistance, supporting local communities, assisting affected populations, and participating in recovery processes. The study’s scientific novelty lies in systematizing CSR criteria by combining universal characteristics of responsible corporate behavior with specific indicators shaped by the wartime environment. Unlike approaches focused primarily on individual social initiatives or general CSR dimensions, the proposed system emphasizes the need to reflect changes in the practical content and priorities of corporate responsibility under extraordinary external conditions. The practical significance of the results depends on the ability to use the proposed system as a basis for further assessment of the level of corporate social responsibility, identification of problematic components, and development of appropriate managerial measures. The proposed approach can also support the development of internal corporate monitoring systems and the selection of relevant indicators according to the characteristics of a particular enterprise, industry, region, and level of war-related risks. Further research should focus on developing a methodological approach to assessing the level of corporate social responsibility and adapting the proposed indicators to sectoral and regional characteristics of business operation during wartime. Keywords: corporate social responsibility; corporate social responsibility criteria; corporate social responsibility indicators; stakeholders; wartime; responsible business behavior; corporate responsibility.

title: Audit Committee Characteristics and Financial Reporting Quality in Kenyan Non-Commercial State Corporations: The Moderating Roles of Accounting-System Automation and Staff Competence
summary: This study examines associations between audit committee independence, diversity, financial competence, meeting practices and the audit-query ratio among non-commercial state corporations in Kenya. It also considers accounting system automation and staff competence as moderators. From 72 targeted corporations, 46 heads of internal audit responded (63.89%). All four committee characteristics were negatively correlated with the audit-query ratio (r = −0.352 to −0.451). Meeting practices showed the most consistent negative association across the reported regression models. The analysis contributes to public-sector accountability research by distinguishing audit-query exposure from broader financial reporting quality and by interpreting the available empirical evidence within its methodological limits. Keywords: audit committee independence; audit committee diversity; financial competence; audit committee meetings; public-sector accountability; financial reporting quality.

title: Incineração de Resíduos Sólidos Urbanos com Aproveitamento para Geração de Energia na Baixada Santista: Controvérsias e Desafios para a Sustentabilidade
summary: The incineration of municipal solid waste (MSW) with energy recovery is presented as an alternative for final disposal, but it generates recurring controversies due to its environmental and health impacts. This article analyzes the debates surrounding the topic based on the Technical Opinion on the Valoriza Santos Waste-to-Energy Facility (URE) and recent scientific evidence. This is a documentary and bibliographic analysis conducted using a qualitative and critical-interpretive approach. The results indicate concerns regarding atmospheric emissions, the release of dioxins and furans, the generation of hazardous ash, and potential adverse impacts on recycling. The discussion contrasts these issues with the scientific literature, highlighting convergences, divergences, and knowledge gaps. It is concluded that the sustainability of the process requires rigorous operational control, lacks alignment with the circular economy, and does not appear to be the most appropriate option within the ESG agenda

title: Digital Business Ecosystem Vulnerability in Africa: A Multi-Method Analysis of Economic Scale and Cyber-Loss Exposure
summary: Africa’s digital business ecosystems are expanding rapidly through mobile banking, fintech innovation, digital payments, e-commerce, and cross-border financial integration. While these developments promote economic growth and financial inclusion, they also increase cybersecurity vulnerabilities across interconnected organisations and stakeholders. This study examines the relationship between economic scale and cybersecurity breach costs across 55 African countries. Using a mixed-methods approach, the research combines qualitative classification of countries according to digital-finance integration with quantitative analyses, including descriptive statistics, kurtosis, and regression modelling. The findings reveal substantial regional variation in cyber-risk exposure, with phishing, malware, business email compromise, and social engineering emerging as the most prevalent threats. The results demonstrate that cyber risk should be understood as an ecosystem-level phenomenon arising from increasing digital interconnectedness among financial institutions, fintech firms, mobile-money providers, governments, and consumers. Regression analysis indicates a statistically significant positive association between GDP and cybersecurity breach costs, suggesting that larger economies generally experience higher financial losses from cyber incidents. However, the findings reflect association rather than causation, as factors such as cybersecurity maturity, digital infrastructure, internet penetration, and regulatory effectiveness may also contribute to cyber-loss exposure. High-GDP countries, including Nigeria, South Africa, Egypt, Morocco, and Kenya, experience disproportionately higher breach costs. The study contributes an ecosystem-oriented framework for understanding cyber-loss exposure and provides evidence to support targeted cybersecurity investment, governance, and resilience-building strategies across Africa.

title: Foreign Aid, Commodity Linkages and African Development
summary: Foreign aid is a paradoxical development tool, especially in sub-Saharan Africa. This article examines the underlying factors shaping foreign aid, highlighting how strategic donor interests often conflict with the developmental needs of recipient states. Using a structured comparative case study of four sub-Saharan African states: Botswana, Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana and Namibia, I argue that foreign aid to specific states reflects the connectedness of the supported sectors to natural resources and commodity markets or supply chains critical to donor economies’ interests. I argue that aid to African states focuses on agriculture, economic development, education and health, as these are the critical areas for Africa. However, donor interests are strongest in African economies, where raw materials are easily accessible to donor states’ markets. In Côte d’Ivoire, donor interests are strongest where agricultural aid is linked to cocoa and cashew production, foreign investment, international trade, and supply chains. Aid to the education and health sectors is influenced by humanitarian reasons, strong, effective institutions, governance, and local ownership of programmes, which strongly influence donor interests. Humanitarian justifications are critical as they provide diplomatic and commercial benefits to donors. I conclude that understanding international relations helps explain foreign aid, and that dependence on commodities is the most significant factor influencing donor interests in providing aid to Africa.

title: Green Digital Transition and Sustainable Technology Supply Chains in the Mediterranean
summary: The rapid expansion of the digital economy poses dual challenges for the Mediterranean region: managing the surging energy and cooling demands of cloud infrastructure and mitigating electronic waste (e-waste) within fragile coastal ecosystems. This paper adopts a comparative qualitative synthesis of publicly available corporate sustainability disclosures, institutional environmental evidence, scientific and policy literature, and European Union regulatory sources to examine how the corporate models of Microsoft Corporation and Apple Inc. interact with sustainability challenges in the Mediterranean context. By contrasting Microsoft’s cloud-first, R&D-driven infrastructure expansion with Apple’s globally distributed, supplier-heavy hardware production model, we analyze key environmental risk vectors – specifically Scope 3 emissions, water scarcity in data center cooling, and e-waste management under the EU Circular Economy Framework. Ultimately, the study offers actionable policy and managerial recommendations for implementing Green IT and sustainable supply chain practices across Southern Europe and the wider Mediterranean policy context.

title: Strategic Decision-Making for Innovation in Emerging Organisations: An Adaptive Framework for VUCA Environments
summary: Strategic decision-making and innovation are critical to the competitiveness of emerging organisations operating in volatile, uncertain, complex and ambiguous (VUCA) environments. This paper examines how emerging organisations can make adaptive strategic decisions while pursuing innovation under conditions of environmental uncertainty. Using O’mari Zimbabwe, a corporate-backed financial technology (fintech) venture of Old Mutual Digital Services, the paper aims to develop an adaptive strategic decision-making framework for innovation in a VUCA environment. The study adopts a qualitative case-study and documentary research design, drawing on publicly available information on O’mari and Zimbabwe’s fintech environment. The analysis applies PESTEL, SWOT, Porter’s Five Forces, stakeholder analysis, and the VUCA framework. The theoretical foundation integrates the resource-based view, dynamic capabilities, organisational ambidexterity, contingency theory, effectuation, bounded rationality, institutional theory, and disruptive innovation. Findings indicate that O’mari’s innovation and competitive advantage depend not only on Old Mutual’s brand, resources, regulatory expertise and institutional legitimacy, but also on its capacity to reconfigure these resources, experiment responsibly, build ecosystem partnerships, strengthen customer trust and continuously learn from environmental change. The paper develops the Adaptive Inclusive Finance Decision Cycle (AIFDC), comprising seven interconnected stages: sensing, problem framing, resource-based option selection, controlled experimentation, trust and regulatory gating, modular scaling, and learning and resource reallocation. The paper concludes that strategic decision-making in emerging organisations under VUCA conditions should be adaptive, iterative, evidence-driven, and innovation-oriented rather than dependent on rigid long-term planning. It recommends strengthening strategic intelligence, controlled experimentation, cybersecurity and responsible data governance, ecosystem partnerships, inclusive distribution, and balanced performance measurement to enhance innovation and competitive advantage.

title: Trade Wars on the Income Statement: The Effects of Tariffs on Firms
summary: We study the firm-level effects of the 2018 and 2025 US tariff episodes. Combining bill-of-lading, supply chain, and financial data, we construct exposure measures across three channels: direct import costs, upstream suppliers' costs, and retaliatory tariffs on exports, validated using stock returns and earnings calls. We provide new evidence that, in 2025, cost exposure reduced sales and variable costs by about 1 percentage point for firms with average tariff exposure, with no margin or investment effects, consistent with demand-driven contractions under constant markups.

title: Logistics Standardisation and Urban Air Quality Improvement: Evidence from Chinese Cities
summary: As urban air pollution control and efforts to improve the quality and efficiency of logistics systems advance in parallel, optimizing logistics operations to improve environmental quality is of considerable theoretical and practical significance. Using China’s logistics standardisation (LS) pilot policy as a quasi-natural experiment, we employ a staggered difference-in-differences (DID) model to examine its effects on urban PM2.5 concentrations, along with heterogeneity, potential channels, and coordination across multiple development objectives. The results indicate that the LS pilot policy significantly lowers urban PM2.5 concentrations, a finding that holds across multiple robustness checks. The reduction is more pronounced in inland cities and those with less developed green finance. Channel analysis indicates that green transportation technology innovation, improved energy use efficiency, and increased local government attention to smart transportation are potential channels through which the LS pilot policy improves urban air quality. Further analysis suggests that the environmental benefits of LS extend beyond air pollution control. The policy significantly reduces urban CO2 emissions, improves the degree of coupling coordination between PM2.5 and CO2 reduction, and increases the overall coupling coordination degree across four subsystems: pollution reduction, carbon reduction, urban greening, and economic growth. By examining urban air quality, this study broadens the evidence on the environmental effects of LS and highlights its potential contribution to pollution control, carbon reduction, and coordinated urban green development.

title: A urgência de uma governança ambiental transnacional׃ uma abordagem centrada na política da agenda climática global
summary: In this paper, we propose a reflection on transnational climate governance as a mechanism for implementing sustainable development. However, the paper discusses the current international system’s inability to articulate concrete public policies capable of dealing with the climate change scenario. From a methodological point of view, the research developed an interdisciplinary bibliographic review, conceiving a holistic dialogue between theoretical perspectives centered on the climate agenda (environmental governance), international public policy and environmental law. The results of the study focused on the criticism of the concept of national borders and their respective jurisdictions, as they have proven inadequate to develop effective models of public policies and regulatory guidelines aimed at consolidating the climate agenda, considering that the biosphere constitutes a unique and interconnected system, transcending the administrative borders of countries. Finally, the research highlights the ineffectiveness of public international law in addressing environmental impacts, since it lacks binding force and remains dependent on the unilateral wills of states, and above all, on the dynamics of the conflicts of government cycles.

title: A Multi-Level Grey Evaluation of the Eco-industrial Development Level of Industrial Parks Based on a Combination of Coefficient of Variation and AHM Weighting
summary: To support environmental management and differentiated green transformation in industrial parks, this study develops an evaluation framework that assesses eco-industrial development performance and identifies park-specific strengths and weaknesses. The framework contains 39 indicators across economic development, ecological environment, material circulation, resource potential, technological innovation, and policy and management. Weights are derived using the Attribute Hierarchical Model (AHM) and coefficient of variation method, integrated via the minimum-deviation principle, and applied through multi-level grey evaluation to four Chinese parks. Findings show that policy and management is weighted highest, followed by economic development and ecological environment; overall performance ranks Tianjin, Suzhou, Dalian, and Fushun. Critically, similar aggregate performance masks distinct weaknesses in environmental governance, resource circulation, technological innovation, and resource conditions. The framework therefore enables diagnosis of differentiated management priorities and supports park-specific pathways toward eco-industrial development.

title: Influence of Quantification of Medical Supplies in Sustainability of Medical Supply Chain in Tanzania
summary: Services, product or supply chain is of utmost importance to any company. This study examining the influence of quantification of medical supplies in the sustainability of medical supply chain in Tanzania. The study utilized a quantitative approach that was paired with a cross-sectional survey research design, the study used a sample size of 150 respondents which included MSD personnel and staff from three medical health facilities. Data gathered from the respondents was analyzed by using multivariate regression analysis and the Statistical Package for Social Science version 32.0 (SPSS) was used to establish the correlation between supply chain factors and the sustainability of MSD’s medical supply chain. The findings revealed that the presence of a substantial relationship between the quantification and the sustainability of MSD’s medical supply chain since the P-values of the four variables drawn from multiple regression analyses were less than 0.05 so P-Values are 0.045 for quantification, while beta are 0.32811. The study concludes that sustainability with quantification, has proved important in the improvement of the entire value chain of medical supply at MSD, helping this institution address previous challenges related to frequent stockouts in healthcare facilities, promote Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), and guarantee the sustainable access and availability of pharmaceutical supplies in health facilities in a cost-effective way. From the key findings of the study, the researcher recommends policymakers should establish clear guidelines and regulations that incentivize and mandate sustainable practices within medical supply chains, managerial inefficiencies should be reduced through effectively engaging with its suppliers in order to identify areas of improvement as well as supplement supply with self-production of some essential medicines. Key Words: Quantification, Medical Supplies, Sustainability, Medical, Supply Chain

title: Advancing resource orchestration theory towards a dual-orchestration framework for digital and green transformation
summary: Abstract Digital transformation and sustainability are increasingly interconnected strategic priorities, requiring firms to address technological and environmental objectives simultaneously. However, resource orchestration research has largely examined digital and sustainability-oriented resources in separate streams, leaving limited understanding of how they can be jointly orchestrated. This study develops a Dual-Orchestration perspective to address this integration gap. A bibliometric analysis is conducted to identify the intellectual structure, major and emerging themes, and thematic evolution of resource orchestration research. The findings reveal growing connections among resource orchestration, digital transformation and technologies, sustainability and green development, dynamic capabilities, environmental uncertainty, resource allocation, stakeholder engagement, and strategic decision-making. Together, these patterns point to an emerging integration opportunity. Building on Resource Orchestration Theory and on the dynamic capabilities, environmental contingency, and managerial cognition perspectives, the study develops a conceptual framework in which digital resource orchestration and green resource orchestration converge through dual-orchestration integration. This integration facilitates the development and deployment of dynamic capabilities, which translate orchestrated resources into sustainable organizational outcomes. The environmental context shapes the relevance and configuration of orchestration, while managerial cognition and strategic decision-making shape orchestration and integration choices. Six conceptual propositions are derived from this mechanism, providing a theoretically grounded basis for future empirical investigation. The study contributes by integrating the fragmented digital and sustainability-oriented resource orchestration streams into a unified perspective that responds to the contemporary need for simultaneous digital and sustainable transformation.

title: Assessing Arab Contributions to Environmental SDGs: Water, Energy, Urban Sustainability and Climate Action
summary: Abstract This study aims to assess and compare the contributions of Arab countries to environmental Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs 6, 7, 11, and 13), and to identify performance gaps, regional disparities, and key policy priorities. The study adopts quantitative and qualitative methods, using secondary data from Voluntary National Review (VNR) reports. A composite Environmental SDG Index is constructed using a standardised 0–5 scoring framework, supported by descriptive statistics, comparative analysis, and thematic interpretation. The results reveal significant disparities across the region, with Gulf countries leading in performance and conflict-affected states lagging behind. Strong progress is observed in renewable energy and urban development, while water management and climate action remain key challenges. The study provides a focused and standardised comparative assessment of environmental SDGs in the Arab region, offering a novel composite index based on VNR data. The findings support policymakers in identifying priority areas for intervention, strengthening environmental governance, and promoting regional cooperation to accelerate progress towards the SDGs.

title: Implementasi Asas Otonomi Daerah Berdasarkan Undang-Undang Nomor 23 Tahun 2014 dalam Penanganan Kebakaran Hutan dan Lahan
summary: Forest and land fires (karhutla) remain a major environmental challenge in Indonesia. This study analyzes the implementation of the regional autonomy principle under Law Number 23 of 2014 on Regional Government in addressing forest and land fires, identifies the challenges faced by local governments, and assesses the effectiveness of regional autonomy in improving coordination, prevention, and mitigation. The research employs a normative juridical approach through library research on legislation, scientific literature, and official government data. The findings indicate that regional autonomy has enabled local governments to establish policies and institutions supporting fire management, including Regional Disaster Management Agencies (BPBD), Fire Control Task Forces, and community-based prevention programs. However, implementation faces obstacles such as limited budgets, human resources, and facilities, weak inter-agency coordination, and low public participation. Regional autonomy has improved coordination and emergency response, yet remains suboptimal due to continued dependence on central government support in technology, funding, and law enforcement. Therefore, strengthening local institutional capacity, cross-sectoral coordination, and community participation is essential for more effective and sustainable environmental governance.

title: Financial Literacy and Green Finance: A Systematic Literature Review
summary: Investments in green projects have become important in the present era due to environmental concerns and the need for sustainable development has arisen. However, the participation of individuals is limited when green projects or green investing is concerned. Financial literacy is one of the reasons which may influence investment in green projects as individuals with financial awareness and financial knowledge are able to make informed investment decisions. It may also depend on individual’s willingness and understanding to invest in green projects. This study will be focusing on examining the relationship between financial literacy and green finance and what factors are held responsible for boosting green investment decision making among individuals. A systematic literature review approach is adopted by examining existing literature from 2010 to 2026 which focuses on sustainable financial literacy, green finance, financial literacy and the factors affecting green investment decision making such as policies awareness, government policies effectiveness, financial awareness programs, environmental awareness and many more. Based upon the literature review, it concludes that financial literacy has strong relationship with green finance but financial literacy is not the only factor which influences green finance there are various other factors which influences investments in green projects like policy awareness, government subsidies, digital financial literacy, sustainable financial literacy, environment awareness, policies effectiveness and fintech adoption. This study also suggests the policymakers to make effective policies which makes active participation in green projects. Secondly, financial education programs should be implemented for adults as well as financial literacy must be taught as a subject to every child through formal mode of education. Thus, this study helps in understanding the factors which influence the relationship between financial literacy and green finance identifies the areas for future research.

title: FIRMS ATTRIBUTES AND FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE OF LISTED OIL AND GAS COMPANIES IN NIGERIA
summary: The study investigates the impact of firm attributes on the financial performance of listed oil and gas companies in Nigeria. Many of these firms have experienced fluctuating profitability, low returns on investment, and earnings volatility due to various operational and economic challenges. This situation raises concerns about whether specific firm attributes contribute to poor or improved financial performance. Factors such as unstable profitability, fluctuating crude oil prices, exchange rate volatility, inflation, and uncertainties in the global energy market significantly affect these companies. The research covers a ten-year period from 2015 to 2024 and includes all five firms listed on the Nigerian Exchange (NE) as of December 31, 2024. Given the available data, the study employed a census sampling approach, examining all five firms in the population. Multiple regression analysis was conducted on the panel data to determine the effects and relationships between the variables. Additionally, correlation and descriptive statistics were utilized. The study recommends that firms enhance their internal financial management practices. While factors such as firm size, growth, capital adequacy, and liquidity exhibited insignificant negative effects on financial performance, it is still essential for firms to maintain adequate liquidity and sound capital structures to ensure operational efficiency and financial sustainability. Regulatory authorities should also promote corporate governance policies. Government agencies and industry regulators should establish policies that strengthen corporate governance and transparency. Moreover, managers should prioritize the efficient utilization of resources instead of merely focusing on expansion, as firm size did not significantly impact financial performance. Emphasizing operational efficiency and productivity improvements is crucial for long-term success. Keywords: Firm Attributes, Firm age, Firm size, Firm Growth rate, Sales growth rate, Capital Adequacy, Leverage and Financial Performance.
