title: A blockchain-enabled U.S. sovereign wealth fund: funding constraints, regulatory barriers, and portfolio implications
summary: The creation of a U.S. sovereign wealth fund (SWF) has long been hindered by fiscal fragmentation, political resistance, and regulatory ambiguity. At the same time, blockchain technology is redefining institutional transparency, asset tokenization, and capital allocation in global finance. This study presents the first empirical simulation of a blockchain-enabled U.S. SWF, evaluating how tokenized asset allocations and on-chain disclosure mechanisms impact risk-adjusted returns and the cost of capital under varying regimes of regulatory and geopolitical uncertainty. Framing the SWF as a politically contingent institutional investor, we assess how financial technologies interact with the U.S. political economy to either amplify or dampen sovereign investment efficiency. Using System-GMM, rolling regressions, and quantile and threshold models across macro-financial data from 2015-2024, we find that Ethereum consistently enhances portfolio performance, but its benefits are highly sensitive to regulatory clarity. In contrast, Bitcoin's volatility renders it unsuitable for sovereign use. These findings underscore how institutional investment outcomes are co-determined by technological design and policy stability, offering new insights into the political economy of sovereign asset governance. Our results speak directly to policymakers, regulators, and institutional investors designing sovereign financial institutions in an era of digital disruption and regulatory flux.

title: Pengaruh Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) dan Karakteristik Perusahaan terhadap Praktik Penghindaran Pajak Perusahaan yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia
summary: Pajak merupakan beban operasional yang mereduksi laba, sehingga memicu manajemen memanfaatkan celah regulasi guna meminimalisasi kewajiban pajaknya. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menguji secara empiris sejauh mana pengungkapan Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) dan karakteristik perusahaan (ukuran perusahaan) mendorong praktik penghindaran pajak tersebut. Berbeda dengan studi terdahulu yang mayoritas berfokus pada dampak variabel terhadap nilai pasar atau harga saham, riset ini menawarkan kebaruan dengan menguji secara komprehensif interaksi antara fleksibilitas struktur internal dan strategi pengungkapan sosial sebagai tameng legitimasi agresivitas pajak. Studi kuantitatif ini menganalisis data sekunder dari 28 entitas di Bursa Efek Indonesia yang ditarik melalui teknik sampling jenuh, serta diolah menggunakan analisis regresi linier berganda. Hasil pengujian membuktikan bahwa intensitas pengungkapan CSR dan skala operasional perusahaan secara parsial maupun simultan berpengaruh signifikan terhadap peningkatan praktik penghindaran pajak. Kesimpulannya, alokasi dana CSR dan pemanfaatan karakteristik internal belum sepenuhnya didorong oleh motif etis, melainkan terintegrasi kuat dengan taktik efisiensi beban pajak. Temuan ini berimplikasi pada perlunya otoritas fiskal untuk menjadikan indikator kepatuhan pelaporan CSR sebagai parameter pengawasan guna mengoptimalkan penerimaan negara.

title: Demand Forecasting for Improving Operational Efficiency in Philippine Department Stores During Holiday Shopping Season: A Theoretical Paper
summary: Demand forecasting represents a significant contribution in improving operational efficiency in retail, in times of customer high demand.In the Philippines, Christmas begins in early September, creating opportunities aiming higher sales but also unveiling challenges such as employee shortages, customer waiting time, excess inventory, and stockouts.This theoretical paper examines the role of demand forecasting in retail operations; the attribute of holiday shopping demand and its connection with inventory management, replenishment, staffing, and supply chain.Furthermore, it discusses ways for improving forecasting precision through previous data, technology, promotional proceedings, and data analytics.In addition, the paper stresses the significance of selecting appropriate forecasting methods based on data quality, business requirement, and demand patterns.By incorporating these methods and dependable forecasts with managerial judgement and operational planning.Department stores in the Philippines can allot resources effectively, control expenses, sustain product availability, and enhance customer service to cater to customers during the Christmas holiday shopping season.

title: Human factor dimensions in industrial maintenance management: a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis (2010–2025)
summary: Introduction This study explores the scientific development of human factor dimensions in industrial maintenance management. As organizations transition toward predictive, digital, and human-centered maintenance systems, human factors such as error, reliability, ergonomics, safety culture, competencies, and human–technology interaction have become central to maintenance performance and industrial safety. Methods A systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis were conducted using 355 documents indexed in Scopus and Web of Science between 2010 and 2025. Data processing, performance analysis, and thematic analysis were carried out in R 4.6.0 within RStudio 2026.04.0 using bibliometrix 5.3.0; VOSviewer 1.6.20 was used only for co-authorship, keyword co-occurrence, and reference co-citation visualizations. A directed qualitative content synthesis complemented the quantitative mapping by examining research streams, mechanisms, gaps, and future priorities. Results Findings reveal a rapidly expanding field, with a compound annual growth rate of 11.69%, particularly after 2019. China, India, and Canada lead scientific production. Co-citation analysis confirms Reason’s human error model as the dominant theoretical reference, while keyword analysis identifies “maintenance”, “human factors”, and “human error” as the conceptual core. Industry 4.0, predictive maintenance, artificial intelligence, and Industry 5.0 emerge as key growth areas. Structured content synthesis identified four interdependent streams: human error and reliability; organizational, ergonomic, and competency factors; workforce planning and optimization; and human-technology interaction in Industry 4.0/5.0. Discussion The results show a transition from retrospective human error analysis toward prospective approaches integrating emerging technologies with human capabilities. The field remains fragmented in terms of authorship and geographically uneven, with Latin America and much of Africa underrepresented. This review positions human-centered maintenance management as an emerging socio-technical field linking human reliability, digital transformation, ergonomics, organizational safety, and workforce development.

title: Factors associated with user satisfaction with government digital services: empirical evidence from Kuwait
summary: Purpose This study aims to investigate factors associated with user satisfaction with digital government services in Kuwait from the users’ perspective and develops and validates an integrated model capturing how service quality, accessibility, usability, security and trust shape satisfaction Design/methodology/approach A quantitative survey was conducted with 378 digital service users in Kuwait. Findings The research identified five key factors associated with user satisfaction: service quality, accessibility, ease of use, perceived security and perceived trust. The study found strong correlations between all five factors and user satisfaction, with perceived trust showing a significant but weaker correlation. However, only accessibility, service quality and perceived security emerged as significant positive statistical predictors of user satisfaction. Accessibility emerged as the strongest statistical predictor. Ease of use and perceived trust did not demonstrate statistical significance in forecasting user satisfaction. Research limitations/implications The study proposed actionable improvements to strengthen digital service design, delivery and assurance in Kuwait, offering practical guidance for public and private stakeholders and helping build user confidence in digital services. Originality/value Research on factors associated with user satisfaction with digital services remains limited, especially in Kuwait. While prior studies have examined selected factors, several potential predictors have been overlooked or treated in isolation. This study contributes to digital transformation scholarship by systematically identifying key statistical predictors of user satisfaction with government digital services in Kuwait and by proposing an integrated model incorporating five factor – service quality, accessibility, ease of use, perceived security and trust – seldom analysed together in earlier research. It provides a practical basis for targeted improvements and future testing.

title: Free Trade Zones, Green Finance Policies, and Corporate Green Transition: Evidence from Chinese A-Share Listed Companies
summary: Against the backdrop of ongoing global green transition and trade liberalization, there remains a lack of sufficient micro-level evidence to determine whether institutional openness can improve corporate environmental performance and long-term sustainable development through the development of green finance. Based on data from Chinese A-share listed companies from 2013 to 2024, this paper utilizes the quasi-natural experiment created by the phased establishment of pilot free trade zones and employs a multi-period difference-in-differences model to examine their impact on corporate green transition and the transmission mechanism of green finance policies. The study found that the establishment of pilot free trade zones has significantly promoted the green transformation of enterprises. An analysis of intermediary effects suggests that green finance policy support may constitute a potential transmission channel; however, since its indicators primarily reflect the intensity of policy activities, they cannot yet directly identify the role of actual financing flows. Further analysis of transmission mechanisms reveals that alleviating enterprises’ financing constraints and attracting long-term institutional investors are key channels for promoting corporate green transition. Additionally, an analysis of spatial effects indicates that the development of pilot free trade zones not only benefits the green transition of enterprises in pilot cities but may also generate positive spillover effects on neighboring cities through cross-regional linkages. This paper reveals the environmental benefits of trade liberalization policies and their financial transmission mechanisms, expands research on the relationship between institutional openness and corporate green behavior, and provides policy insights for emerging economies seeking to balance economic openness, environmental protection, and sustainable development goals. However, as the study sample primarily consists of Chinese listed companies, the cross-national applicability of the findings requires further verification.

title: Green Signal and Global Sales: The Impact of Environmental Accounting Disclosure on Export Performance of Small Cap Firms in South Africa
summary: Small and medium enterprises are an essential part of any economy as a result of their contributions to the economic output. However, the export performance of small businesses, especially in developing countries, is limited by environmental regulations enacted to achieve sustainability goals due to compliance costs. Moreover, there is a paucity of studies on how environmental disclosure practices impact the export performances of SMEs. Hence, this study investigates the effect of environmental accounting disclosure on the export performance of 15 small-cap companies in South Africa between 2015 and 2024. Using panel regression analysis, the result showed that environmental accounting disclosure (EAD) exerts a significant and negative impact on export revenue. Also, firms’ size (TA) has a direct and significant relationship, while market capitalization and leverage variables have no significant effect on export performance. In addition, the effect of exchange rate is positive and significant on export revenue. This study concludes that there is a possibility that the resource and compliance demand associated with environmental disclosure may be burdensome for export oriented small businesses in South Africa. Hence, the results from this study contradict the prediction of positive link proposed by Signalling theory and Resource based view. Therefore, there is a need for a supportive policy framework that will enable small cap exporters to pursue environmental transparency without weakening their international competitiveness.

title: The In-Depth Challenges and Opportunities of Enterprise Digital Transformation
summary: In the digital era, digital transformation can be regarded as a "reconstruction of the underlying architecture" of an enterprise's management system. With the increasing maturity of technologies such as big data, artificial intelligence, and the Internet of Things, traditional product and service models have struggled to form effective competitiveness. As a result, digital transformation has evolved from an "optional choice" to a "mandatory requirement" critical to the survival of enterprises. In the process of transformation, enterprises are faced with challenges not only at the technical level, but also in the overall upgrading of skill structure and organizational capability from the management level to each business department. This paper systematically analyzes the common problems in the digital transformation of enterprises, puts forward corresponding solutions, and discusses the internal mechanism of digital transformation to promote the long-term development of enterprises.

title: Fuzzy–AI digital twins for sustainable, resilient food supply chains
summary: This study proposes a prescriptive Fuzzy–AI Digital Twin framework for food supply chains operating under deep uncertainty. The digital twin streams real-time operational data from production, cold storage, transport, and retail into a learning optimization loop. Uncertainty in demand, lead times, capacities, spoilage, and emissions is modeled using adaptive fuzzy sets, while a deep-learning surrogate accelerates a multi-objective NSGA-II optimizer to co-design decisions across cost, CO₂e, and resilience. In a perishable dairy case, the hybrid approach reduces total cost by 12.2%, lowers emissions by 15.2%, and raises the resilience index by 22.5% relative to the Fuzzy–AI model without Digital Twin integration. The optimizer stabilizes in ∼35 generations, and under severe disruptions the network recovers to 95% capacity in ∼5 h (vs. >10 h traditionally). Conceptually, the framework operationalizes resilience via adaptability (sensing disruptions, simulating alternatives, and reallocating resources in real time) rather than costly redundancy. Managerially, it enables simulate-before-implement orchestration and transparent cost–carbon–resilience trade-offs aligned with Scope-3 reporting. The results indicate that digital twins combined with fuzzy reasoning and learning assisted optimization can deliver simultaneously lower cost, lower emissions, and higher resilience for perishable food chains.

title: Enabling or weakening? Artificial intelligence and ambidextrous green innovation
summary: Purpose This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI) adoption shapes firms' ambidextrous green innovation by inducing differential effects on exploratory and exploitative activities from an attention-based perspective. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the attention-based view, we theorize that AI adoption reconfigures organizational attention and technological capabilities, leading to divergent effects on green innovation. Using panel data from Chinese listed firms, we employ regression analyses to test these arguments. Findings AI adoption exerts a double-edged effect on ambidextrous green innovation. It significantly promotes exploratory green innovation by redirecting managerial attention toward forward-looking strategic issues, while suppressing exploitative green innovation by institutionalizing routine processes and reducing sustained attention to incremental improvements. Furthermore, Confucian cultural embeddedness, negative media coverage and institutional ownership strengthen the positive effect of AI on exploratory green innovation and mitigate its negative effect on exploitative green innovation. Practical implications These findings suggest that managers should align AI adoption with balanced attention allocation to avoid overemphasizing exploratory innovation at the expense of incremental improvements. Originality/value This study advances the literature by conceptualizing AI as an attention-restructuring mechanism that systematically differentiates firms' exploratory and exploitative green innovation. It contributes to research on AI and organizational ambidexterity by uncovering the contingent role of institutional and social contexts.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Financial Reporting: Transforming Customized Financial Statements, Decision Intelligence, and Assurance Practices
summary: Financial statements are prepared from trial balances that have passed internal-control checks and, for external reporting, have been audited before stakeholders rely on them. Converting this verified ledger into the views needed by investors, creditors, regulators, and management remains largely manual, causing rework, delays, and duplicated reconciliation. This study designs and evaluates an artificial intelligence (AI)-coordinated architecture that generates stakeholder-specific yet reconciled reports from a single governed trial balance. Following a design science approach, the architecture combines centrally configured accounting policies and KPI definitions, lineage metadata, account classification, anomaly detection, sequence forecasting, financial natural language processing (NLP), role-aware customization, and human-in-the-loop explainable AI (XAI). The prototype was evaluated on 15,000 trial balances for 500 entities (12,000 synthetic and 3,000 derived from public SEC filings) against rule-based, robotic process automation (RPA), and commercial generative-AI baselines. It achieved a line-item disclosure fidelity (F1) of 0.965, an AUC of 0.97 for misclassification detection, and a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 4.8% for one- to four-quarter forecasts; in 250 simulated multi-entity scenarios, preparer effort fell from 38.0 to 4.2 person-hours per reporting cycle. Simulated stakeholder and auditor responses illustrate the expected gains in perceived usefulness and trust. Limitations include synthetic and statement-derived data, simulated rather than observed perception measures, and an unevaluated narrative-generation module.

title: Operationalising the impact-finance protocol: institutional architecture and the role of DLT in digital sustainable finance
summary: Sustainable, impact and development finance increasingly rely on digital systems to measure and manage real-world social and environmental performance. Yet impact information is still used primarily for reporting and retrospective assessment, rather than as an operational input into financial decision-making. This creates a persistent gap between what financial systems know about real-world outcomes and how capital is actually allocated, released or constrained. This study examines how that gap might be addressed through the Impact-Finance Protocol (IFP), an institutional architecture designed to connect trusted real-world information with financial execution. Building on the conceptual IFP proposed in earlier work, the study evaluates how the protocol behaves when operationalised under real implementation conditions. A comparative Design Science approach was used, combining an initial reference implementation with a longitudinal programme of implementation across multiple institutional, governance and technical contexts. The protocol, rather than any individual organisation, technology or project, was treated as the unit of analysis. Implementation evidence was systematically reconstructed through evidence validation, qualitative coding, implementation-episode reconstruction, comparative analysis and Design Knowledge synthesis. The findings show that the core responsibilities for structuring evidence and verifying its meaning remain comparatively stable across different implementation contexts. By contrast, connecting verified information to financial action requires more extensive governance, institutional authority and operational coordination than the original architecture anticipated. Practical implementation also depends on cross-cutting capabilities such as legal identity, compliance, financial accounts, payment rails and coordination across recurring and overlapping implementation processes. Community participation emerges as an operational capability, while system-level Assessment remains comparatively immature and requires further implementation and evaluation. Where distributed ledger technology (DLT) mechanisms were used, they supported selective integrity, coordination and governed execution, but remained context-dependent rather than necessary architectural components; off-chain verification, institutional authority and governance remained fundamental to financial activation. The study contributes implementation-derived Design Knowledge and transferable Design Principles for digital sustainable finance. It shows that enabling trusted impact information to influence financial decisions requires not only reliable data and verification, but an institutional architecture capable of governing how information becomes actionable financial value across diverse real-world settings.

title: THE CROSS-BORDER MIGRATION OF CHINA'S DIGITAL GOVERNANCE EXPERIENCE UNDER THE CHINA-ASEAN DIGITAL ECONOMY COOPERATION FRAMEWORK
summary: With the rapid development of digital technology, digital governance has become an important path to modernizing national governance and a key issue in global economic cooperation. Within the framework of China-ASEAN digital economy cooperation, regional cooperation practices centered on the "Digital Silk Road" have provided fertile ground for the cross-border transfer of China's digital governance experience. This paper, from the dialectical perspective of "development empowerment and sovereignty balance," systematically examines the core elements, current status, and pathways of the cross-border transfer of China's digital governance experience. The study finds that China's digital governance model, characterized by state-capacity leadership, infrastructure exports as a precursor, the promotion of technical standards as a link, and multi-party collaborative governance as a mechanism, has generated significant spillover effects in ASEAN's digital transformation process. This cooperation not only provides ASEAN countries with a development path different from the West and innovates the South-South digital cooperation paradigm, but also injects new momentum into the equitable and diversified transformation of the global digital governance system, highlighting the global governance significance of the "Chinese solution."

title: Impact of global supply chain pressures on energy demand and stability: The role of global sustainability initiatives
summary: Global supply chain pressures (GSCP) have become a major challenge for multinational enterprises (MNEs), influencing firm-level operational decisions, including evolving energy demand patterns. This paper investigates the impact of global supply chain pressures on energy consumption in Chinese MNEs from 2013 to 2022. Results from Double-Selection Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) linear regression indicate that GSCP increases the energy demand of Chinese MNEs. One possible explanation is that GSCP undermines production stability and operational efficiency, prompting firms to intensify production, extend operating hours, and adopt additional shifts to meet volatile demand conditions. Furthermore, global shocks (i.e., US-China Trade War and COVID-19) and global green initiatives (i.e., Montreal Protocol–Kigali Amendment, the EU Innovation Fund, and the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative) significantly moderate the relationship between GSCP and energy demand. The heterogeneity analysis exhibits that the GSCP impact is most pronounced among state-owned MNEs, firms with substantial overseas investment experience, and enterprises exhibiting lower degrees of internationalisation. This study contributes new empirical and theoretical insights into how global supply chain disruptions affect corporate energy demand and shape the strategic responses of Chinese MNEs.

title: Blockchain Enabled Decentralized Nuclear Waste Supply Chain Management
summary: As nuclear waste has long-term effects on the environment and society, managing it safely and effectively is a major global concern. Conventional nuclear waste management systems may face challenges related to record keeping, transparency, and reliance on manual monitoring, potentially affecting operational efficiency and stakeholder confidence. This study presents a blockchain-based platform designed to enhance accountability, data integrity, and traceability in nuclear waste management procedures. The proposed system leverages the decentralized and tamper-resistant nature of blockchain technology to record and track waste-related information throughout its lifecycle. It provides a user-friendly interface to support interaction among stakeholders, including waste producers, storage facilities, and the general public. The system's development and testing demonstrate the implementation of blockchain-based record keeping, waste tracking, and sensor data monitoring. These functionalities provide a foundation for maintaining verifiable records and improving the visibility of waste management activities. Although the current evaluation demonstrates the system's functional capabilities, further comparative testing is required to quantify improvements in data integrity, traceability, and operational efficiency over conventional approaches. This project contributes to ongoing efforts toward safer and more sustainable nuclear waste management by presenting a potential solution that can be further evaluated and adapted for other hazardous material management applications.

title: Inclusive Organizational Infrastructure and Supply Chain Operational Value through Coordination and Integrative Capability
summary: Abstract Debate over whether diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) belongs in the operational core of the firm has intensified rather than settled because of an unresolved analytical problem: the operations and supply chain management (OSCM) literature documents that inclusion is associated with organizational outcomes without specifying the operational machinery producing that association. We reframe inclusion as inclusive organizational infrastructure - the configuration of workforce diversity, structural equity and inclusive culture that determines whose knowledge legitimately enters operational decision processes - and model its conversion into operational value as a translation architecture. Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory, supported by inclusion climate, social capital and relational view arguments, we theorize that inclusive infrastructure activates three distinct coordination mechanisms (internal, inter-organizational and boundary-spanning), that these crystallize into integrative operational capability, which is converted into operational value realization. Survey data from 264 food export enterprises in Vietnam and China were analyzed using covariance-based structural equation modeling, bootstrapped mediation decomposition, measurement-invariance testing, multi-group analysis and necessary condition analysis. Coordination and integrative capability jointly transmit 47.2% of the total effect of inclusive infrastructure on operational value, with inter-organizational and boundary-spanning routes carrying most of the indirect effect. Network coordination complexity negatively moderates the capability-to-value relationship, and multi-group evidence indicates that the conversion of inter-organizational and boundary-spanning coordination into capability is significant only under low complexity while the direct infrastructure-to-value relationship persists, a pattern we term compressed capability translation . Necessary condition analysis shows that integrative capability is a degree-dependent prerequisite, not merely a predictor.

title: Hyperbolic Discounting and Short-Term Bias in Reverse Logistics Capital Allocation for Circular Supply Chains
summary: The government's short-term focus by executives slows down funding for circular supply Chain because it focuses only on the short-term benefits. We examine managerial present bias (β_”proxy”) and capital allocation using Tobit, Panel Fixed Effects and Cox hazard models of 1,872 supply chain deal transactions (2015-2024) obtained from IFC and World Bank databases. The risks of project cancellation increase significantly as the project pays back over a longer period of time (HR=1.482, p<;0.001), and reverse logistics are adversely affected by the project payback time more than forward supply chain. Committed capital (b=0.318, p<;0.001) and allocation (b=0.128, p=0.003) are higher with reduced present bias and with blended finance, respectively. Under-investment is due to internal choice architecture, not lack of capital.

title: Post-harvest stages account for more than half of seafood carbon footprint
summary: Abstract Seafood is increasingly important for healthy dietary transitions in modern urban lifestyles. Yet, the patterns of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions remain poorly understood, which hinders the low-carbon pathways for city-specific seafood supply chains. Here, we constructed a disaggregated supply chain dataset to quantify the GHG footprint of consumption of five major seafood categories across 313 Chinese cities. In 2023, total GHG footprint of Chinese seafood consumption reached 182.6 Mt CO₂-eq (1.5% of the national total emissions), dominated by shellfish (65.7%) and fish (25.1%). Annual per-capita emissions varied from over 1000 kg CO₂-eq/capita in coastal and tourism cities to near zero in many inland cities. Spatially, 79.9% of emissions were concentrated in coastal cities, with the top five cities contributing 27.2%. Most transported seafood (58–88%) was within 200 km, indicating shorter food miles than other food categories. We find that off-farm supply chain stages, which account for 55% of total emissions, are key to retaining seafood's low-carbon advantage over terrestrial protein sources such as chicken and pork. We highlight the need for coordinated strategies to support both sustainable and healthy diets, including efficient mariculture practices in coastal cities and low-carbon cold-chain logistics and feed production in the supply chain.

title: A Multilevel Socio-Technical System: Formation of Government Financial Reporting Quality in China—Survey Evidence from the 2019 Accrual Accounting Reform
summary: Using questionnaire data collected in 2019, this study examines how preparation conditions relate to perceived government financial reporting quality (GFRQ) in the first year of China’s new government accounting system. The multilevel socio-technical systems (MSTS) framework distinguishes departmental reporting as an operational layer and consolidated reporting as an integration layer. Separate respondent-level regressions use 5157 departmental and 672 consolidated questionnaires; they estimate associations within each report type, without testing interactions or information transmission between layers. Policy cognition and institutional support, and information systems and data integration are positively associated with GFRQ in both samples. Accounting foundation and accrual implementation are significant in the departmental sample. The prespecified coordination and supervision index is positive in both baseline models, although departmental inference is sensitive to scoring. These findings describe preparation conditions and quality evaluations in the 2019 survey. Comparisons across report types are descriptive; coefficient equality has not been formally tested. Cross-layer transmission and feedback remain theoretical propositions, while suggestions on responsibility tracing, reconciliation and error correction are directions for subsequent evaluation. The results are bounded by the survey’s institutional and technical context and do not establish later reform outcomes or current governance performance.

title: Integrated diagnostics of adaptive digital transformation in FMCG retail
summary: The article develops an integrated diagnostic model of adaptive digital transformation in FMCG retail aimed at identifying imbalances between technological development, organizational capabilities, and market outcomes. The proposed approach combines four interrelated diagnostic contours: external digital opportunities, actual technology adoption, internal digital readiness, and customer and market response. The research is based on system, process, comparative, and structural-logical approaches, as well as analysis, synthesis, classification, and scientific generalization. The empirical illustration of the model uses publicly available corporate data for 2025-2026 covering ten Russian FMCG retail chains. Digital readiness is assessed through four components: management commitment, digital potential, digital culture, and digital strategy. The results indicate that relatively balanced average levels of digital readiness coexist with noticeable firm-level differences in their internal configuration. Digital culture demonstrates the highest average value (0.885), whereas digital strategy has the lowest (0.840), suggesting that the development of technological and organizational capabilities may outpace their integration into a coherent long-term transformation agenda. To translate diagnostic results into managerial decisions, a matrix linking specific diagnostic signals with corresponding management responses is proposed. The developed framework supports the identification of capability bottlenecks, underused technologies, customer-journey friction, and inconsistencies between digital readiness and actual technology adoption. Its practical application can facilitate the prioritization of digital initiatives, continuous monitoring, strategic adjustment, control, and recurrent recalibration of digital transformation trajectories in FMCG retail enterprises.

title: Pharmaceutical Shortages as a Multi-Level Governance Failure: An Exploratory Multi- Stakeholder Qualitative Study with Implications for EU and UK Policy
summary: Abstract Background Medicine shortages increasingly threaten patient safety and health system resilience across high-income countries. Despite expanding literature on supply chain vulnerabilities, the perspectives of frontline professionals, such as pharmacists and clinicians, remain underrepresented, and the multi-level governance dimensions of shortage management remain underexplored. Methods We held a participatory multi-stakeholder workshop in March 2025 at the Università di Bologna, Italy. Eighteen participants from the UK and Italy took part in structured presentations and facilitated discussions. They included clinicians, pharmacists, procurement specialists, policymakers, industry representatives, and academic researchers. Recordings of the discussions were transcribed, anonymised, and analysed using thematic analysis in NVivo 15, with themes interpreted through a multi-level governance framework. Results Five themes were identified: diversification and cooperation; transparency and trust; regulatory frameworks; demand-side pressures and public messaging; and national and regional security. Participants highlighted geographic concentration of manufacturing, fragmented supply chain communication, and rigid regulatory frameworks as structural causes of medicines shortages. Frontline professionals, particularly community pharmacists, were identified as bearing the greatest operational burden of shortages while having the least regulatory flexibility to respond. Proposed responses included expanded domestic manufacturing, real-time inventory systems, reformed procurement criteria, greater pharmacist dispensing flexibility, and strengthened international coordination. Conclusions Our findings indicate that pharmaceutical shortages represent a systemic, multi-level governance failure rather than a purely logistical problem. Effective responses require coordinated action across supranational, national, and local levels. This should include regulatory reform such as expanded pharmacist dispensing flexibility; improved transparency and incentive-based early notification; and strategic investment in supply chain resilience to facilitate cross-sector stock redistribution. Reshoring and diversification strategies must also engage with the environmental governance implications of where and how medicines are manufactured. Our findings provide preliminary practitioner-informed evidence relevant to EU and UK policy developments to address medicine shortages, including the Critical Medicines Act (CMA), while highlighting persistent gaps in their scope.

title: Shifts in the Semiconductor Supply Chain: An Analysis of TSMC’s Fab Locational Decisions
summary: Relations between China and Taiwan have been fraught since the Chinese Civil War, when Taiwan became independent from the People’s Republic of China (PRC). The PRC views Taiwan as a part of mainland China, an ongoing sovereignty debate that has left many third-party actors to ambivalently declare allegiance to China to maintain trade relations while also maintaining informal ties with Taiwan. Many countries in the West ideologically align with Taiwan but have no formal diplomatic ties to the country. The Taiwan question has been answered with strategic ambiguity since the Chinese Nationalist Party (KMT) fled China. During the 1970s and 1980s, Taiwan’s technology sector grew, along with Taiwan’s national identity. Over this period of economic growth, the semiconductor manufacturing industry became largely concentrated in Taiwan. Foreign countries, which all have economic development stakes in the semiconductor industry, also began to have increased stakes in a country they do not even formally recognize. To make matters more complex, the PRC has economic ties to all these countries, which are now reliant on Taiwan’s semiconductor manufacturing industry and its leader Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC). The PRC itself depends on TSMC and Taiwan’s robust semiconductor industry to manufacture its semiconductor chips’. This creates a problem in international relations because states must determine how to conduct economic transactions with a company with ties to a state they do not even formally recognize. Additionally, the significant bargaining power of a single company, TSMC, raises important considerations for the future of technology development, international economics, and international peace and security. My research seeks to analyze TSMC’s corporate strategy and understand its rationale for placing its fabs more clearly. Examining the various economic and political factors will yield insight into TSMC’s supply chain diversification strategy.

title: Explaining the Decline of Natural Wealth per Capita: A Three-Pillar ESG Analysis of the World Bank Wealth Accounts
summary: Comprehensive wealth accounting defines net investment in natural capital as the change in the stock, yet country-level ESG research has concentrated on flow measures of environmental pressure and left this outcome unexamined. Drawing on the World Bank Sovereign ESG Data Portal, this paper takes the annual change in renewable natural capital per capita, from the Changing Wealth of Nations accounts, as its dependent variable, for 149 to 151 countries between 1995 and 2020. It is explained three times, through parallel equations differing only in the ESG pillar of origin of their regressors, so that the three sets of determinants are estimated as distinct and comparable effects rather than compressed into a composite index. Each equation is developed through panel econometrics across six estimators, a comparison of six clustering algorithms ranked on eleven internal validity indices, and six supervised learners used to validate the specification rather than to predict. Median renewable natural capital per capita falls by 29.7 per cent and its share of comprehensive wealth halves, yet the aggregate stock is roughly constant: the coefficient on population growth is −0.913, indistinguishable from the value implied by the accounting identity, and becomes insignificant on the total stock. The decline is therefore demographic arithmetic. Climatic stress is the most robust environmental determinant, and its coefficient more than doubles when agricultural land is excluded from the dependent variable. Institutional trajectory dominates institutional level, a distinction recovered independently by the clustering. Relationships differ systematically between the two panel dimensions, and the renewable energy share reverses sign across them.

title: Mapping the Software Supply Chain Security Landscape: A Full Corpus Synthesis
summary: The software industry is confronting a critical crisis driven by systemic vulnerabilities within the software supply chain and the ubiquitous reliance on third-party dependencies. While individual exploits and localized compliance frameworks have been heavily studied, this highly fragmented academic discourse creates a critical barrier to organizational readiness and proactive incident preparedness. To address this gap and enhance digital resilience, this study maps the conceptual, knowlegde and structural landscape of software supply chain literature using Synthetic Knowledge Synthesis. Analyzing publications from 2021 to 2026, the research reveals an exponential growth in output, heavily dominated by conference proceedings and driven primarily by institutional and state-funded efforts in the United States and China. Thematic mapping identifies five core clusters defining the current ecosystem: Software Composition Analysis, Advanced Vulnerability Detection, AI-Driven Threat Intelligence, Deep Learning, and DevSecOps. The study highlights critical unresolved gaps, notably the prevalence of false positives in static Software Bill of Materials tools due to a lack of execution context, and a pronounced disconnect between theoretical models and practical enterprise application. Future research directions emphasize the integration of Large Language Models for automated patch generation, the development of execution-aware vulnerability triage, and the evolution of dynamic, AI-driven artifacts to secure complex dependency networks.

title: GREEN SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT AND FIRM PERFORMANCE IN E-COMMERCE ENTERPRISES
summary: Drawing on the resource - based view and natural resource - based view, this study examines how green supply chain management practices influence the performance of e - Commerce enterprises. This study conceptualizes green supply chain management through five di mensions: intra - organizational environmental management, product eco - design, green supplier integration, green customer cooperation, and reverse logistics. The study further investigates the role of environmental performance in improving operational, econo mic, and social performance. Using a quantitative approach with partial least squares structural equation modeling, the study collected survey data from 162 managers and employees in e - Commerce enterprises. The results indicate that all five dimensions of green supply chain management practices positively affect environmental performance. Environmental performance subsequently enhances operational, economic, and social performance, while operational performance significantly and positively affects economic performance. However, social performance does not directly affect economic performance. The study contributes to theory by extending the resource - based view and natural resource - based view to the underexplored e - Commerce context. The results also suggest t hat e - Commerce enterprises should invest in eco - design, environmental management systems, supplier collaboration, customer engagement, and reverse - logistics capabilities to improve sustainability and competitiveness.

title: Sustainable Procurement and Supply Chain Localization under Saudi Vision 2030
summary: Sustainable procurement in Saudi Arabia has become a practical mechanism for linking industrial competitiveness, domestic value creation and responsible supply-chain performance. This structured narrative review examines how purchasing governance, supplier development, local content measurement and sustainability criteria can be combined within energy and infrastructure supply chains under Vision 2030. Drawing on public policy documents, institutional reports and relevant procurement research published principally during 2020–2025, it distinguishes localization outcomes from purchasing preferences and considers their operational trade-offs. The review identifies five interacting dimensions: transparent sourcing, supplier capability, lifecycle value, responsible production and measurable domestic economic contribution. It proposes a staged framework linking demand forecasting and supplier qualification to collaborative capability building, contract execution, independent measurement and continuous improvement. Evidence from Saudi Arabia’s industrial-development initiatives and Aramco’s In-Kingdom Total Value Add program indicates the strategic importance of domestic manufacturing, technical skills, innovation and supplier diversification. However, local purchasing alone does not demonstrate sustainability or resilience; firms must also assess delivery reliability, labor safeguards, environmental performance, competitiveness and the quality of local value creation. The article develops an implementation scorecard and research agenda for evaluating localization without sacrificing project schedule, safety or public value.

title: From orchestrated resources to supply chain performance: the indirect role of power
summary: Purpose The study applied resource orchestration and resource dependency theories to examine how firm resources affect supply chain performance in Ghana's food and beverage industry, as well as the mediating role of power. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach and explanatory design were employed using survey data collected from firms in Ghana's food and beverage sector. Out of the 427 questionnaires distributed, 395 usable responses were obtained. The data were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling to assess direct and specific indirect effects. Findings The results indicate that human, financial and innovation resources significantly enhance supply chain performance, whereas relational and structural resources do not exert direct effects. Power positively influences performance and serves as a critical mechanism, with both partial and full mediation observed across resource categories. The findings reveal that resource value is heterogeneous and context-dependent, and that performance gains are realised when resources are effectively translated into influence that aligns with partner behaviour. Originality/value The study advances the literature by moving beyond the composite view of firm resources and demonstrating that resource effects are not uniform but context-specific. It further positions power as a central mechanism linking resource deployment to performance, offering a more context-sensitive explanation of supply chain dynamics in developing economies.

title: How carbon border adjustment mechanism awareness shapes export strategic responses in Vietnam’s high carbon-emitting industries
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine the associations between Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) awareness, perceived compliance costs, green supply chain management, green innovation, export competitiveness and export performance among Vietnamese exporters. It also assesses whether measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) capability and government support condition selected relationships. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 227 firms in CBAM-exposed, carbon-intensive industries were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). Robustness tests added firm-level controls, and multi-group analysis compared small, medium-sized and large firms after measurement invariance assessment. Findings CBAM awareness is positively associated with perceived compliance costs, green supply chain management and green innovation. Green innovation has the strongest positive association with export competitiveness, whereas perceived compliance costs are negatively associated with competitiveness. The aggregate green supply chain management–competitiveness relationship is non-significant but masks a negative coefficient for small firms, a positive coefficient for medium-sized firms and a negligible coefficient for large firms. Export competitiveness is positively associated with export performance. Originality/value Rather than proposing a general theory of CBAM, the paper contributes a firm-level, CBAM-specific dual-pathway model in Vietnam. It shows how an institutional awareness construct is associated concurrently with a compliance-cost pathway and an innovation pathway, while firm-size heterogeneity qualifies the aggregate evidence.

title: Carbon Emission Disclosure, Environmental Disclosure, Capital Intensity, and Corporate Financial Performance in Indonesia
summary: Purpose: This study analyzes the effect of carbon emission disclosure, environmental disclosure, and capital intensity on the financial performance of energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2020–2024.Research Methodology: This quantitative study uses the annual and sustainability reports of 38 companies selected through purposive sampling, yielding 190 firm-year observations. Carbon emission disclosure and environmental disclosure are measured with 18-item and 31-item indices, capital intensity with fixed assets to total assets, and financial performance with an adjusted return on assets series. The Random Effect Model is selected through the Chow, Hausman, and Lagrange Multiplier tests in EViews 12.Results: Carbon emission disclosure (B = 1.825225; p < 0.001) and environmental disclosure (B = 1.297164; p < 0.001) are positively and significantly associated with financial performance, whereas capital intensity is not significant (B = 0.027686; p = 0.8971). The three variables are simultaneously significant (F = 65.21017; p < 0.001), with an adjusted R² of 0.504757.Conclusions: Transparent carbon and environmental reporting is associated with stronger financial performance, whereas the proportion of fixed assets alone does not differentiate performance among energy companies.Limitations: The study covers one sector over five years, measures disclosure breadth rather than quality, and relies on an adjusted performance series that cannot be fully reproduced.Contributions: This study integrates stakeholder value-creation, legitimacy, signaling, and agency theories by demonstrating how carbon and environmental reporting jointly signal financial performance, providing insights for Indonesian firms, investors, and regulators.

title: Reframing Corporate and CSR Governance With Contexts in Mind: Why We Need to Restore the G to the B&S Field
summary: ABSTRACT The Business & Society field concerns itself with improving relationships among the overlapping spheres of business, society, and the natural environment to create shared value. This paper argues that the field needs to focus more on the potential of government in reshaping corporate governance and corporate social responsibility (CSR) multistakeholder governance institutions and practices to head off impending or future tragedies of the commons. The legal construct of corporate personhood has incentivized business executives to define their responsibilities narrowly in terms of profitability and asset appreciation. CSR stakeholder network governance arose from activist efforts to forge standards of social and environmental performance that can win voluntary corporate accountability and compliance. The problem is that global “corporate citizens” have been reluctant to devote resources beyond what is needed to achieve the credible appearance of compliance with voluntary sustainability standards. This paper uses the potential of a tragedy of the commons scenario to consider how we can head off a potential dystopian future posed by an AI Armageddon.

title: DEVELOPING BUSINESS CULTURE AMONG UNIVERSITY STUDENTS IN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY
summary: This article examines the development of business culture among students in the context of the digital economy. It highlights the importance of economic thinking, entrepreneurial skills, digital literacy, and business ethics. The paper also analyzes challenges in higher education and proposes measures to strengthen startup ecosystems and enhance practice-oriented approaches.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Accounting: Applications, Benefits, Challenges and Future Prospects
summary: The swift advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is revolutionizing conventional accounting practices by facilitating enhanced automation, precision, efficiency, and data-informed decision-making. AI tools are progressively utilized in various fields such as bookkeeping, financial reporting, auditing, fraud detection, tax management, financial analysis, and forecasting. It is crucial for accounting professionals, organizations, educators, and students to comprehend these applications as the accounting field continues to evolve with technological progress. Even though previous research has looked at the potential of AI in accounting, more knowledge is still needed about how AI is being used in various accounting activities, the advantages it offers, and the obstacles to its adoption. More research is needed on issues pertaining to data protection, cybersecurity, implementation costs, ethical concerns, transparency, and the evolving skills needed for accounting professionals. This study's primary goal is to investigate the use of artificial intelligence in accounting and to evaluate its main advantages, difficulties, and potential. Based on secondary data gathered from scholarly publications, professional reports, research papers, and other pertinent sources, the study uses a descriptive research methodology. The results show that AI may enhance financial decision-making, decrease tedious human labour, increase fraud detection, and speed and improve accounting procedures. However, the right technology infrastructure, qualified personnel, moral principles, and efficient data governance are necessary for successful deployment. According to the study, AI should be seen as a supplement to accounting professionals rather than a replacement for them. To prepare professionals for the future of accounting, accounting companies and educational institutions should concentrate on building technical, analytical, and ethical abilities relevant to AI.

title: Forensic Accounting in the Digital Asset Era: A Structured Framework for Bitcoin Verification and Investigation
summary: The rise of blockchain-based digital assets presents significant challenges for auditors tasked with ensuring compliance with the International Standards on Auditing. Traditional audit methods are often ill-equipped to address the decentralised, pseudonymous and cryptographically complex nature of the asset class. This study develops an Assertion-based Audit Framework as a structured audit artefact tailored to the technical attributes of the Bitcoin blockchain. Using a methodology embedded in the design sciences paradigm, this research applied an elaborated Action Design Research approach to iteratively design and validate the audit framework in collaboration with industry professionals. It translates blockchain protocol features, such as unspent transaction outputs, public and private key cryptography, and decentralised ledger systems into assertion-level audit procedures covering existence, rights and obligations, completeness, valuation, accuracy, occurrence and cut-off. As illustrated in the simulated context, the envisaged audit framework aims to provide reliable and reproducible evidence, thereby strengthening the audit quality and forensic investigations involving bitcoin. This research advances both academic and professional knowledge by offering a formalised, technology-integrated audit framework, with broader implications for auditing digital assets across various blockchain protocols – supporting both regulatory-compliant financial audits and forensic investigations conducted where robust and verifiable evidence is essential.

title: The Impact of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Performance on Corporate Return on Investment: Evidence from China
summary: Improving corporate return on investment and generating returns for shareholders are among the important operating objectives of listed companies. With the development of the stakeholder concept, corporate operations have paid greater attention to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance; however, whether ESG performance can improve return on investment remains to be studied. Using a sample of Chinese A-share listed companies from 2009 to 2023, this study constructs a two-way fixed-effects model to examine the relationship between corporate ESG performance and return on investment. The empirical results show that ESG performance can significantly improve corporate return on investment, and this result remains valid after a series of robustness tests. The heterogeneity analysis finds that the positive effect of corporate ESG performance on corporate return on investment is more significant among non-state-owned enterprises, large firms, and young firms. The mechanism tests show that ESG performance can improve corporate return on investment by increasing total factor productivity and promoting corporate green innovation. This study provides empirical evidence from Chinese listed companies for understanding the economic consequences of ESG performance and also provides a reference for firms seeking to improve operating performance.

title: Digital Transformation in Healthcare: Implications for the Professional Practice of Radiologic Technologists
summary: Digital transformation in healthcare is reshaping the role and responsibilities of radiologic technologists, yet empirical evidence on how Filipino practitioners perceive and adapt to this shift remains limited. This descriptive–correlational study, Digital Transformation in Healthcare: Implications for the Professional Practice of Radiologic Technologists, employed a validated survey questionnaire distributed to 45 radiologic technologists in selected hospitals and diagnostic imaging centers to assess the extent of digital transformation, its implications on workflow, job roles, and required competencies, as well as the associated challenges and opportunities. Findings indicate that foundational digital infrastructures, such as Picture Archiving and Communication Systems (PACS) and Radiology Information Systems (RIS), are already well‑established, with an overall mean of 3.05 (interpreted as “Significant”). In contrast, AI‑integrated modalities and advanced automation tools remain less developed. The implications of digital transformation on professional practice were rated “Very Significant” (overall mean = 3.38), with shortened turnaround times and expanded responsibilities in informatics and data management as the most notable changes. Challenges, including system downtimes, network glitches, and increased cognitive workload, were also rated “Very Significant” (overall mean = 3.43). The study concludes that digital transformation is already advancing in radiologic practice and proposes a Digital Transformation Readiness Framework for Radiologic Technologists to enhance diagnostic accuracy, patient safety, and professional autonomy, ensuring that technological change strengthens—rather than diminishes—the human‑centered, ethically sound practice of the profession.
